entries.not_relevant_because: The family is a single preprint, 'A Counterexample to Kurosh's Division-Ring Problem', which constructs a countable characteristic-zero division ring that is algebraic over its center, generated by two elements over it, and infinite-dimensional over it. Its subject is local finiteness of algebraic division rings (Kurosh's problem), not nil one-sided or two-sided ideals of arbitrary rings as in the Köthe conjecture. A text search of the build/ sources finds no mention of Köthe or of one-sided or two-sided nil ideals; the only nil-related remark (introduction, Golod's nil algebras) concerns non-division algebras and is set aside as not answering the division-ring question. Division rings have no nonzero nilpotent elements, so the Köthe implication holds trivially for them and the construction says nothing about the general ring-theoretic statement.
